note: Sets out twelve components of a psychological audit, which is one of the few published specifications of what an AI audit should contain.
title: Auditing the AI auditors: A framework for evaluating fairness and bias in high stakes AI predictive models.
explain_beginner: AI systems often make important decisions about people, like who gets a job or a loan. This paper asks a simple question: how do we check whether those systems are fair? The authors propose a checklist with twelve parts for auditing AI. Some parts look at the AI itself, including its data and design. Other parts look at how the AI is explained to the people who use it and the people affected by it. A few parts apply to everything, like cultural context and respect for people. This matters because it gives a structured way to catch bias.
explain_business: This paper offers a practical checklist for auditing AI systems that make decisions about people. It defines twelve components across three areas: the model itself, how the model is communicated to users and affected people, and overarching concerns like cultural context and respect for persons. For executives, it means fairness reviews can follow a defined structure rather than an ad hoc process. The decision it informs is how to scope an AI audit before deployment in high stakes settings, and what evidence to require from vendors about data, design, and claims.
explain_practitioner: The authors present a standardized audit approach for evaluating fairness and bias in AI systems that predict human outcomes. They specify twelve components grouped into three categories. The first covers model aspects: source data, design, development, features, processes, and outputs. The second covers how information about models and applications is presented and understood by deployers, affected individuals, and third party observers. The third covers meta components applied across all others: cultural context, respect for persons, and integrity of research designs behind developer claims. The key contribution is one of the few published specifications of audit contents.
